alpha-unique.comment: LOWERED on 2026-08-16, 4758015856 to 3703471500 instructions. The wire decoder decided a tag by asking petta_py_tag/2 whether it was o, then s, then g, then n, re-running atom/1 and string/1 at every step, so a single ['n',1] leaf cost nine inferences to recognise. Normalising the tag once and dispatching on it lets first-argument indexing pick the clause: a number leaf falls to 4.00 and a three-element expression 29.00 to 20.00. Attributed by interleaved A/B of that change alone, min-of-3 instructions:u: 4133301509 to 3703607237, -10.40%. This workload evaluates one large nested term per operation, so the per-node saving compounds over every node crossing the wire. LOWERED again on 2026-08-16, 3703471500 to 3587525535, and the drop is not a speed-up: this case is now measured in STEADY STATE. benchmarks/pure.py runs its operation once before the counters start, so the engine's one-time global-stack growth is no longer inside the measured interval. That growth was the whole of the bimodality recorded below.
alpha-unique.instruction_noise_comment: LOWERED back to 1.0 on 2026-08-16, matching every other bench, because the bimodality it was raised for is GONE rather than tolerated. benchmarks/pure.py now warms this case up, which was named as the sharper fix when the 12% was recorded, and it holds: adding ten inert clauses to src/python.pl used to move the count from 4176751912 to 3772644013 and back, alternating, three rounds, and with the warm-up the same two trees measure 3587527424 and 3585946931, a 0.05% step instead of a 10.7% one. The warm-up is per case, declared in pure.py's _WARM_UP, because a warm-up changes what a workload MEANS wherever its second run differs from its first: source-load run twice measures redefining a thousand equations rather than defining them. Two attributions made against the old 12% ceiling are void, and are corrected in ai-design-grounded-view.md: neither the writer's clause shape nor the tuple guard's allocation was worth the 400 million instructions claimed for it. Both changes are still right on their own terms; only the numbers were cluster assignment.

annotated-relation.comment: Raised on 2026-08-19, +4,998 (+1.04%), by keying a function's retained equations (fun_meta_clause/4 in src/translator.pl) by MODULE as well as by name. Keyed by name alone, two spaces defining one function shared one pile of equations and the specializer built one clause per equation in the pile, so a space answered its query twice because a SIBLING space happened to use the same function name; measured at c7126f1 as well, so it is older than the module migration [tested: specializer_invalidation:a_definition_in_another_space_does_not_double_an_answer, which goes red against the name-keyed read]. The cost is 4.00 inferences per compiled CALL SITE, not per equation, because specialization_plan/5 asks which module it is compiling for before it reads the equations, so the raise tracks each lane's call-site count: handle-round-trip 1950079 to 1990079 over 10,000. Two cheaper shapes were measured and rejected on this lane: spelling the module read out inline instead of calling current_metta_module/1 saves 4,000 (1986079) and is not worth duplicating a published service's body for 0.2%, and collapsing fun_meta_clauses/3's owner probe into a single findall over the current module costs 124,004 (2114083), because an inherited function's equations live in &self's module and that shape then walks the chain on every call. Minimum of three. Prior: Raised from 479523 on 2026-08-19, +2,498 over 500 evaluations, +5.00 each. Raised on 2026-08-19 by Phase 11, which gives every space its own execution module, &self included, so an equation can no longer replace a predicate the engine resolves. Two mechanisms, both attributed by interleaved A/B against c7126f1 on the same box: space_module/2 costs one inference more, 4.00 against 3.00, because it maps a space to a module through a computed name and a cache where it used to answer with the space's own atom; and with_metta_module/2 costs one more, 11.00 against 10.00, for the guard that refuses a SPACE where a module is asked for, which is what turns a silently wrong module context into a refusal now that the two are different atoms. A whole runnable form measured 372 against 369 inferences, one space_module/2 and two with_metta_module/2. current_metta_module/1 (4.00), reduce/3 on a builtin (20.00) and get-type (29.00) are unchanged, because metta_self_module/1 and metta_exec_module_prefix/1 are inlined by goal_expansion/2 rather than called. Two cheaper shapes were measured and rejected: asserting the known spaces as facts of space_module/2 itself reads one inference less and leaves a choice point that took eval-arith from 172,009 to 237,980 inferences, and spelling out eval/2's own module read bought nothing. Prior: Raised on 2026-08-18: the Python library's run() and load() now run the engine's own pre-pass over a parsed source before processing any of its forms (prepare_parsed_forms/1 in src/filereader.pl), so a ! may name a function the same source defines lower down; without it seven shipped examples passed in the engine and failed in the library. A one-form source costs 31 inferences there, measured identical for !(+ 1 2), the collapse-top form and the foreign match. This lane runs 500 of them: 464021 to 479523, 31.004 per evaluation. The committed ceiling was 465021, 1000 above the arm-A floor, so the gate saw +14502 of the +15502. Prior: Raised from 464021 on 2026-08-18, +2 per evaluation: the price of the named-space wrapper fix. timeout, elapsed, take, top, transaction and the bound forms hand their goal to helper predicates, and those are meta_predicate now, so the goal keeps its module and the six forms work in named spaces at all (they answered Unknown procedure for any MeTTa-defined function there before). This lane runs (top 1 ...) in a named space 500 times, so it pays the Module:Goal wrap per evaluation; translate-time baking was measured as the alternative and cost +5 per evaluation on this same lane (466519), so the wrap is the cheaper correct form. Prior: Raised from 461521 on 2026-08-17, +998 from the &self reader cascade on its five hundred directives (see run-source) and +498 from petta_on_error_mode/3's petta_ctx_declared/1 precondition: this space declares annotations, so the flag check succeeds and adds one inference per on-error consult before petta_shape_route runs as before. That precondition is CA-7's trade: a ctx with no declarations at all now skips the shape route entirely. Both shares measured by hot-swap differential, 461015 to 460017 to 460517 [measured 2026-08-17]. Prior: The Empty prune's gate and walk beside each collapse, dated 2026-08-17; see run-source for why the filter is not in the findall goal. Raised from 463023 on 2026-08-18, the engine prelude: compile-path type-chain lookups gained the prelude masking tier (~1 inference per miss), and the counter wobbles up to 6 across invocations from dynamic-register JIT index timing, so this is the max observed minimum across the gate and bare-shell contexts.

direct-join.comment: Raised from 280275 on 2026-08-19, +20137 (+7.18%), 2.01 inferences per answer row: a conjunctive match now finds every row BEFORE any output template runs. The language requires that, "match first finds all the matches, and then instantiates the output pattern with them, which is evaluated outside match", and this engine reversed ONE link of upstream's three-link loop example because each later conjunct was a fresh goal reading the space after the previous row's template had written to it. The rows are collected through findall/member, so the cost is one copy and one unification per row and tracks the join's row count and nothing else: the slope lane sees the same 2.01. A space whose declared semiring is bool skips the per-row annotation capture, which was another 3 per row before it was guarded [measured 2026-08-19: 320322 with the capture on every row against 300412 without]. Not reducible here: taking one answer is observably the same lazily or eagerly, since one template cannot disturb a later conjunct, but match/4 is not told a bound applies, so (once (match &s (, ...) ...)) now walks the join; pushing the bound through the snapshot needs the translator to carry it. Prior: Raised from 270305 on 2026-08-18, +1 inference per answer row: the occurs-check correctness fix. petta_py_row now guards its bindings with acyclic_term/1 once per row, because a rational-tree join sailed past match_native's out-template guard (the bindings live outside the template) and died in the row encoder at a 53-million-frame walk; a register_prolog predicate can bind X=f(X) into a row, so the guard cannot be dropped even though native_expression now occurs-checks each candidate too. Attribution: the delta is exactly repeats*rows, 9970 over 5*1994 [measured 2026-08-18].

json-wire.comment: RE-FLOORED 2026-08-17 from 3753315597: the codec changed, not the cost of the old one. dumps and loads now cross into the engine and run library(json), so one round trip pays two janus crossings and two Prolog passes, 62M instructions per trip against the removed orjson path's 1.9M, a factor of 33 on this bench. That is what frees the name, and it is most of the collision surface: measured through the shipped guard, register_op/2 refused 237 of the 465 names the library's boot imports at MeTTa arity 1 and refuses 4 of 469. The cost is the space_module/2 read the probe, the refusal, the registration and the unregistration each now do, plus asking BOTH tiers whether a name is still defined, which is not optional: current_predicate/1 with the arity unbound enumerates a module's own predicates and not the ones it reaches through its base chain, so asking either tier alone released a name the other still defined. save-load-fast.instruction_comment: ADDED on 2026-08-16. This benchmark had an inference baseline and no instruction one, and it is the byte-copying path: it writes a whole 20,001-atom space to a file as text and reads it back. typed-call.instruction_noise_comment: RAISED to 5.0 on 2026-08-17, from the 1.0 every other bench carries, because this workload's instruction count is LAYOUT-sensitive at 3.13% and nothing in the tree selects the mode. Ten clauses that NOTHING CALLS, appended to src/python.pl, moved it from 6590121734 to 6390136042, and removing them moved it back. A sweep of the same probe reads 6590121734, 6558144686, 6462134810, 6518142057, 6438133781, 6390136042 at 0, 1, 2, 3, 5 and 10 clauses, saturating there and unchanged at 20, so it is a continuum rather than the two modes alpha-unique had [measured 2026-08-17]. The INFERENCE count is identical across every one of them, which is what says no logical work ever changed. This is code-layout bias, the effect Mytkowicz, Diwan, Hauswirth and Sweeney measured in 'Producing Wrong Data Without Doing Anything Obviously Wrong!' (ASPLOS 2009), where link order and environment size alone move a benchmark by several percent and can reverse a conclusion. alpha-unique's warm-up does NOT fix this one: with typed-call added to pure.py's _WARM_UP the same two trees still measure 6591481484 and 6391492325, so the mode is not the one-time stack growth that was, and the warm-up was reverted rather than left in for nothing. The allowance is measured rather than guessed, and the ceiling still sees what it exists for: this bench is gated in instructions because the inference counter cannot see the type-check specialisation, and disabling that specialisation by one token measures 9368378515, +42.2% against a 3.13% noise floor, a 13x margin [measured 2026-08-17]. The baseline stays at the LOW end of the layout range rather than being re-recorded at the tree's current value, so a real regression sitting on top of the high mode still fails.

wire-codec.comment: RAISED on 2026-08-19, 3457164978 to 3467063880, +0.286%, from Expr's lazy _wire slot on a workload that now CHAINS its trips. The workload changed in the same commit and the change is the honest half of that number: it used to re-encode one long-lived atom 2000 times, which the new slot answers from cache after the first, and the lane reported -31.61% for a change that stopped encoding rather than encoding faster. Each trip now encodes the atom the previous trip decoded, so encoding stays cold and the +0.286% is the slot's real cost on a cold crossing. Prior: LOWERED on 2026-08-19, 3522689581 to 3457054691. Same change as term-operators: Expr writes its slots through their descriptors. Attributed by interleaved A/B, 3536110132 to 3457065051, -2.24%. from_wire builds one Expr per decoded node, so this lane pays the two writes 51 times per trip.

counter_policy: stats().inferences minimum of three and fixed two-point growth slopes decide; wall time advises
instruction_policy: perf instructions:u minimum of three, one percent noise allowance, measured under a deterministic harness since 2026-08-17: the child environment is a fixed allowlist, PYTHONHASHSEED is 0, and setarch -R disables address-space randomization, because environment-block size, hash seeds and ASLR each selected alignment modes that moved counts up to 1.5% with the inference counter flat. All floors re-measured under that harness on 2026-08-17.
